resources.string: Fast, highly accurate English model with punctuation and capitalization (~600MB)
Supports 25 European languages (~600MB). Long internal pauses or quiet/noisy padding can lose speech; use shorter recordings.
Required to detect focused text fields and insert dictation
Required to show the floating dictation button
50–150% of the original size. Changes apply immediately. Drag partly beyond any screen edge; a small part stays reachable.

Spelling only: capitalizes or joins/splits spaces in text with identical recognized letters. Acoustic custom-word recognition is not restored: the bundled decoder can repeat words or lose speech with contextual boosting. Your saved terms are retained.

Enabled by default for um, uhm and uh. Edit one word or phrase per line, then Save. Matches whole words without case sensitivity, never parts of real words. Only final text changes, across floating, live and file dictation. Clear the list or switch off to keep everything. Settings are read when transcription begins.
Words or phrases to remove (one per line)
Use up to 100 entries, each up to 80 characters: letters, numbers, spaces, apostrophes or hyphens. No regular expressions.

Acoustic context boosting is currently unavailable because native probes found repetition and lost speech. Saved names and technical terms remain available for optional spelling-only hints; these cannot add words or correct sound-alike recognition. This is not a replacement for acoustic custom-word recognition.
No custom vocabulary added yet. Add optional spelling hints above.
No transcriptions recorded yet. Focus any text field across the system and tap the floating dictation button.
Voice Dictation Accessibility Service detects when text input fields are focused to display the floating dictation button and directly injects recognized speech into the active text field.
